title: Persist monitor layout with xorg.conf
summary: Configure monitor positions and resolutions permanently by creating an Xorg configuration file. This applies the layout at every boot.
prerequisites: You know the monitor identifiers (e.g., VGA1, HDMI1) from 'xrandr -q'.

steps.explain: Create a configuration file for monitor layout. This example places HDMI1 to the left of VGA1. You must restart X (log out and back in, or reboot) for changes to take effect.
steps.gui:
Create a file named /etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/10-monitor.conf with the following content:

Section "Monitor"
    Identifier  "VGA1"
    Option      "Primary" "true"
EndSection

Section "Monitor"
    Identifier  "HDMI1"
    Option      "LeftOf" "VGA1"
EndSection

rollback.explain: Remove the file /etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/10-monitor.conf using a file manager or terminal.

warnings: Incorrect configuration can prevent X from starting. Keep a backup of your current config.
